report.tagline: Valve's online store and app where PC gamers buy, download, play and talk about games.
report.simpleSummary: Steam is the main shop for PC games. You install the Steam app, buy games, and they download and update by themselves. Your games stay in your account forever, and you can play with friends, read reviews and buy during big seasonal sales. Valve, the company behind it, keeps about 30% of every game sold, and also makes the Steam Deck handheld.

overview.whatItDoes: Steam is a digital store, game library and social network for PC and Steam Deck players. Developers publish their games on it and Valve handles payments, downloads, updates, anti-piracy and community tools. Players get one place for all their games, friends and reviews.
howItWorks: A player makes a free Steam account and installs the Steam app on PC, Mac, Linux or Steam Deck.
They browse the store, see user reviews and wishlists, and buy with card, UPI-linked cards, PayPal or Steam Wallet.
Games download from Valve's servers and update automatically.
Developers pay a $100 fee per game to list, then Valve keeps 30% of sales, falling to 25% after $10 million and 20% after $50 million per game.
Big seasonal sales (Summer, Winter, Spring) and festivals drive huge spikes in buying.
Community features like reviews, Workshop mods, groups and the Steam Market keep players engaged.
overview.valueProposition: For players: one library for life, fair user reviews, huge discounts and friends in one place. For developers: access to the biggest PC audience with payments and tools handled.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Players rate games up or down and can refund within 14 days if played under 2 hours.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Builds trust so players buy more, and pushes developers to ship good games.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Players save games they want; Steam recommends new games.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Wishlists notify buyers on launch and sales, the biggest driver of indie sales.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Store-wide discounts like the Summer Sale and Next Fest demos.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Creates buying events and pulls in lapsed players.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Players share mods and trade in-game items, with Valve taking a fee on trades.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Keeps old games alive and adds extra revenue.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A handheld PC running SteamOS, with Proton making Windows games run on Linux.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Grows play time outside the desk and reduces reliance on Microsoft Windows.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Achievements, cloud saves, matchmaking and anti-piracy for developers.

After 10 hours, posts a thumbs up.

businessModel.summary: Steam makes money mainly from a cut of every game sold, usually 30%. It also earns from in-game purchases made through Steam, fees on Community Market trades, its own games like Counter-Strike 2, and hardware like Steam Deck.

revenueStreams.detail: 30% of each sale, dropping to 25% after $10 million and 20% after $50 million per game. Average around 24% in 2025.
Valve takes a cut of microtransactions processed through Steam.
Counter-Strike 2 and Dota 2 earn from cases, skins and battle passes.
About 15% on item trades between players.
Steam Deck, and Steam Machine, Steam Frame headset and Steam Controller due in 2026.

businessModel.pricing: Free to join. Games priced by developers, often with regional prices such as ₹499 to ₹3,999 in India. Steam Deck OLED from about $549 in the US.
costDrivers: Bandwidth: players downloaded about 100 exabytes in 2025
Engineering for store, client, SteamOS and Proton
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $30 indie game, Valve keeps $9 and the developer gets $21. Valve pays maybe 3% to 5% for payments and a little for bandwidth, so it keeps roughly $7 to $8. Valve has only a few thousand employees, so most of that falls to profit, which makes Steam one of the most profitable businesses per employee in tech. Steam Deck is likely sold at a small profit or near cost to grow play time. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Free-to-play hits like Counter-Strike 2 and Dota 2
Developers sending players to Steam because their game is only there
Seasonal sales covered by gaming media
Steam Deck bringing new handheld players
whatBringsUsersBack: Library and friends list already there
Achievements, trading cards and seasonal events
growth.moat: Players have years of games in their Steam library and friends on Steam, so leaving is costly. Developers go where players are, and players go where games are. Epic gave away free games for years and still did not break this loop.

pmLessons: Trust features like honest reviews and easy refunds can raise sales, because buyers worry less.
A two-sided marketplace is very hard to dislodge once both sides are locked in, even by a rival giving games away.
Running buying events like seasonal sales creates habits and spikes that keep a store top of mind.
Owning your hardware and operating system, like Steam Deck and SteamOS, reduces dependence on another company.

interviewQuestions.question: Epic charges 12% and gives free games, yet Steam still wins. Why?
interviewQuestions.hint: Talk about network effects, library lock-in, features, and trust. Price is not everything.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve game discovery on Steam?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment players and developers, list signals (play time, friends, wishlists), propose a feature, define metrics like conversion from discovery.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Valve launch a Game Pass-style subscription?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh more play time against lower developer revenue and cannibalising sales. Run a small test.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Steam?
interviewQuestions.hint: Hours played, broken into active players, hours per player, purchases and developer supply.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Steam in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Regional pricing, UPI payments, smaller downloads, cafes and laptops, local free-to-play games.

glossary.meaning: The share of each sale a platform keeps for itself.
The number of people using a service at the exact same moment.

When a product gets more useful as more people use it.
Something that makes it hard for a competitor to copy a business or win its customers.
The one number a team focuses on because it best shows the value users get.
The share of people who take a next step, like buying after viewing a page.
Laws that stop a company from unfairly using its size to block rivals.
Small purchases inside a game, like skins or extra levels.
When leaving a product is hard because your stuff only works inside it.

assumptions: Steam's yearly sales and December revenue are third-party estimates; Valve does not publish revenue.
Valve's profit per game sold is estimated from known cut rates and typical payment costs.
The figure of about 19,000 new games a year is based on 2024 to 2025 trackers.
Steam Deck profit margin is not public.
